_comment: THE SEED, not the live config. On a deployed box IG_RULES_FILE points at
/var/lib/ig-automation/rules.json, which is written by the admin panel at
/admin/ and copied from this file only the first time, when nothing is there.
Editing this file changes nothing on a running install.
Rules are ordered and the FIRST match wins, so put specific keywords above
media: { mode: 'all' } fires on every post. { mode: 'only', ids: [...] }
narrows a rule to particular posts, which is how one keyword can mean
NEVER put a rule's own keyword inside its publicReply. We post that reply,
Meta hands it back as a NEW comment with a NEW id, it matches again, and the
account answers itself until Instagram throttles it. The dedupe table cannot
catch it — every loop step has an id it has never seen. The panel refuses to
save it and the service refuses to start quietly on it.
Meta allows exactly ONE private reply per comment, ever — dm.text, dm.link
and any uploaded dm.fileId are concatenated into that single message, so it
has to carry the whole payload.
